title: Retry: handler throws retryable error re-delivers via applied queue with attempts counter
asA: developer authoring a job that can fail transiently
iWant: the applied queue to redeliver a failed message per the job's elicited retryPolicy within the applied queue's max-attempts ceiling, with the attempt counter incrementing on each jobStarted event
soThat: transient failures self-heal within maxAttempts and terminal failures are recorded once via jobFailed with a terminal error code

acceptanceCriteria.description: With SIMULATE_HANDLER_THROW=true set on the shared sample-app fixture, the retry-and-fail probe schedules a job whose handler throws a retryable error; the applied in-memory queue redelivers the message per retryPolicy.maxAttempts. Three jobStarted events fire on the sink with the same jobId and attempts counter 1, 2, 3; after the third failure jobFailed fires with a terminal error code and no further re-delivery follows.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the fixture with SIMULATE_HANDLER_THROW=true and the retry-and-fail probe running against the in-memory queue seam
acceptanceCriteria.then: three jobStarted records with the same jobId and attempts 1,2,3; one jobFailed with a terminalErrorCode; no fourth jobStarted

acceptanceCriteria.description: Handler timeout raises a retryable error. Given a handler exceeding the elicited handler-timeout-seconds without completing, when the runtime wall-clock reaches the timeout, then the runtime raises a retryable timeout error routed through the applied queue redelivery, jobFailed fires with { jobId, reason: "timeout" }, and the message is redelivered against maxAttempts.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a handler exceeding the elicited handler-timeout-seconds
acceptanceCriteria.then: a retryable timeout error routes through the queue; jobFailed fires with reason: timeout; the message is redelivered

acceptanceCriteria.description: Retry backoff exponential effective-delay per attempt is base * 2^(attempts-1) capped at 10 minutes. Given a job with retryPolicy.backoff='exponential' and base=1 second, when the runtime issues retries for attempts 1..15, then the effective inter-attempt delay observed on the sink is 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, 16s, ..., 512s, then capped at 600s (10 minutes) for every subsequent attempt; a probe measuring the schedule spacing FAILS if any attempt spacing exceeds 10 minutes or does not follow the 2^(n-1) curve until the cap.
acceptanceCriteria.given: retryPolicy.backoff='exponential' with base=1s and maxAttempts sufficient to reach the cap
acceptanceCriteria.then: inter-attempt delays observed on the sink follow base*2^(attempts-1) up to 600s then cap at 600s; the cap probe FAILS on any spacing above 10 minutes

acceptanceCriteria.description: Retry backoff constant effective-delay per attempt equals base seconds. Given a job with retryPolicy.backoff='constant' and base=5 seconds, when the runtime issues retries for attempts 1..N, then every observed inter-attempt delay on the sink equals 5 seconds and the probe measuring the schedule spacing FAILS on any observed delay that deviates from base by more than the sink's tick resolution.
acceptanceCriteria.then: every observed inter-attempt delay equals 5 seconds; probe FAILS on any deviation beyond the sink tick

acceptanceCriteria.description: Retry backoff linear effective-delay per attempt is base * attempts. Given a job with retryPolicy.backoff='linear' and base=2 seconds, when the runtime issues retries for attempts 1..N, then the observed inter-attempt delay on the sink is 2s, 4s, 6s, 8s, ..., growing linearly; a probe measuring the schedule spacing FAILS on any spacing that does not equal base*attempts within the sink tick resolution.
acceptanceCriteria.then: observed inter-attempt delays follow base*attempts (2s, 4s, 6s, ...); probe FAILS on any deviation
